note: THE SOURCE for the company's site. Every fact the site states about the company is said here, once. What it states about the product - the version, the licence, the commands it names, every feature and every release - is the engine's, read from the release requirements-engine.txt pins, and never typed here. A null is a fact not decided yet: the page leaves out what depends on it. The demo, and the questions under Why Wherefore, are an illustration - an example company's plan and the assets that state it - and the pages say so; `{name}` in a line is a value the generator fills from beside it, so no number is said twice. The case study's counts are not here at all: the pendulum counts them itself, facts/pendulum.json is the copy, and each stat names the count it shows by `of`.

why.heading: Why “Wherefore”
why.juliet: Juliet wasn’t asking where Romeo was. She was asking why he had to be who he was.
why.rule: In a Wherefore repository every file has to answer her: generated from a source, written by a person for a stated reason, or captured and stamped with what it was made from. A file that cannot answer stops the change.

asks.name: {after}
asks.because: Customers kept calling them projects; only we said workspace. The reason was written down with the change, so it ships with it.

asks.name: demo video
asks.because: My script and captions are built from the same names as the app, so I never point at a button the product no longer has.

asks.name: slide 4
asks.because: I read the same names and claims as the feature pages, so the slide and the site cannot drift apart.

asks.name: orange
asks.because: The accent is said once. Every page, slide and social card is built from it, so a rebrand is one line.

asks.name: “SOC 2 certified”
asks.because: I am not allowed yet. Until the audit is signed, the most any page may say is “SOC 2 in progress”, and the check refuses the rest.

why.note: The same example company as the demo on the home page.

words.scan: Point it at your site or docs. It finds every value you say two ways.

words.gate: On every push, each file is built from a source, written for a reason, or stamped. Nothing else ships.
words.build: Every asset rebuilt from the source, the same way every time.
words.proofs: No check is trusted until it has failed: each proof plants the fault its check catches.
words.retired: Retire an old price or name once; nothing a person reads may say it again.
words.reach: Each fact is moved, one at a time, and everything that states it must change.
words.claims: Give a claim like “SOC 2 certified” a rule; no page can say more than it allows.
words.upstream: Copied a partner's spec? The deploy fails the day their source changes.
words.published: A page on a CMS nobody builds? Declare what it states. Wherefore reads it live and fails when it disagrees.
words.hook: A push that would ship a stale document stops before it leaves your machine.
words.skill: Claude Code or Codex learns the rules from a skill that ships with each release.
words.docs: Every release ships its own docs, held to its code by tests; this site shows its release's.
words.graph: Every file, how it is made, and what moves when a source does, on one page.
words.palette: Your brand's colours live in one file. A colour typed anywhere else fails, by file and line.
words.report: Stuck? One command writes the report, nothing private in it, and sends it to us.
words.pins: A new release? Your repository sees it, moves the pin and opens a pull request. No token, no client list.
words.scan2: Your site, app, backend and docs scanned together, and where any two disagree.
words.scan-read: Beside the result: what each place read, what it left unread, and the colours it states.
words.drift: Hand-written files that state a value no source holds, named and counted. The allowance only falls.
words.launch: Everything you call ready has a stage, and it moves only when it has what it needs.
words.status: Where a repository stands, in one read: its files, its drift, its launches, its engine.

case.name: Chaotic Pendulums
case.heading: A hardware company, built from one spec file.

model.title: The MK3 pendulum in 3D: drag to turn it, or grab an arm and swing it

case.text: Chaotic Pendulums builds a desk-sized double pendulum from one spec file: drawings, print files, parts list, supplier pack and website. If one source can hold machined parts, it can hold your app and docs.
made: Part drawings a machine shop quotes and inspects against, each with its cut file and its solid model
Print-ready 3D files for a prototype, laid out plate by plate
A bill of materials, and a quote bundle a shop’s online tool takes in one drag
The engineering hand-over, frozen at every release so a shop can always find the pack it quoted
The brand: the mark, the hero and the renders, drawn from the object’s own dimensions
The website, and the 3D pendulum that swings on it
held: Load simulations, worked from the real parts’ masses, prove every mount setup holds the pendulum at a torque a hand can give.
Worst-case tolerance stacks prove every screw clamps and never bottoms, at every extreme of every band.
A sweep proves the blade turns a full circle and touches nothing.
The swing on the website is integrated from the physics of the object as it is today, and a check holds every mass and length to the parts.
